finding.claim: The admin check in ban() is swallowed by a broad try/except, so any authenticated non-admin caller can ban arbitrary users via POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban.
finding.source: Caller identity via g.user (set by upstream middleware not in repo) and the uid path parameter.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the ban action.

trace.note: Route POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban registered; no decorator-level guard.
require_admin(g.user) is called inside the handler.
For a non-admin, require_admin calls abort(403), raising HTTPException.
except Exception catches the HTTPException, which subclasses Exception.
Only log.warning is emitted; no return or re-raise.
Execution continues to do_ban(uid), performing the ban.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) enforces the check but its 403 is discarded by the except at line 18. No decorator, before_request, or blueprint guard visible. unban (admin.py:24-28) calls require_admin without try and correctly propagates 403. If g.user is None, AttributeError is raised and the log line also raises outside the handler, returning 500 without banning, so exploit requires g.user to be a dict with falsy is_admin. do_ban is a stub here (pass), so real impact depends on its full implementation.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) raises abort(403), but its exception is caught and discarded by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18, so it does not block do_ban at admin.py:20. The unban handler (admin.py:26) calls require_admin without a try and is not affected. No decorator, before_request, or other guard exists in the repo (only admin.py is present).
verdict.reason: The 403 raised by require_admin at admin.py:11 is swallowed by the except at admin.py:18, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any caller whose g.user has a falsy is_admin. Caveat: do_ban is a stub at admin.py:31-32, and the upstream middleware that sets g.user is not in the repo, so the authentication requirement and real impact are not verifiable here.
